tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear Path for Target Disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move a disk that is not on top, you must first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to other pegs, ensuring the target disk becomes the topmost and can be moved legally. This step respects the rule that only the top disk of a peg may be moved.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has one or more smaller disks stacked on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 5 is at the bottom of a peg with disks 2 and 1 above, first move disk 1 and then disk 2 to other pegs before moving disk 5.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Build Goal Stack in Decreasing Size
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Assemble the final tower on the goal peg by placing disks from the largest down to the smallest, never putting a larger disk on top of a smaller one. This ordering guarantees the final configuration satisfies the size constraint.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final stack on the target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To achieve [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2, first move disk 5, then disk 4, then disk 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Phase Planning (Move‑k‑Disks)
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a sub‑problem of moving k disks by recursively moving the top k‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the kth (largest) disk to its destination, and then moving the k‑1 disks onto it. This divide‑and‑conquer approach reduces a complex move sequence to simpler, repeatable steps.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to relocate a contiguous block of the smallest k disks as part of a larger plan.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move three disks from peg A to peg C using B as auxiliary, first move the top two disks to B, then move the third disk to C, and finally move the two disks from B onto C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a small disk onto the goal peg before all larger disks that must sit below it have been placed there. Placing a small disk too early blocks later placement of larger disks and can create illegal configurations.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a move would put a small disk onto the final peg while larger required disks are still elsewhere.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not move disk 1 onto the goal peg before disks 5, 4, and 3 have been positioned there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Legal Move Invariant
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Every move must satisfy two conditions: the source disk is the topmost disk on its peg, and the destination peg is either empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. Maintaining this invariant guarantees that all moves obey the Tower of Hanoi rules.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before executing any move, check both the source and destination constraints.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 sits on top violates the invariant; you must first move disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat Existing Goal Disks as Fixed Base
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Once a disk is correctly placed on the goal peg and all larger disks beneath it are also correctly placed, treat that stack as immutable and never move those disks again. This prevents undoing progress and simplifies subsequent planning.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After a disk has been placed in its final position and all larger disks below it are already fixed.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After moving disk 5 to the goal peg, never move disk 5 again while building the rest of the tower.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Exploit the Smallest Disk’s Flexibility
tower-of-hanoi.principle: The smallest disk can be placed on any peg without violating size constraints, making it an ideal temporary buffer for shuffling other disks or freeing pegs. Use it to create space for larger moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a free peg or must temporarily clear a peg while preserving legality.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Move disk 1 to an empty peg to free the top of another peg for moving disk 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Post‑Construction Verification
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After generating the complete move list, replay the moves from the initial configuration to verify that each move is legal and that the final configuration matches the goal. This catch‑all check catches any overlooked errors.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have produced a candidate solution, before submitting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Simulate the 20 moves in the solution and confirm the final state is [5,4,3,2,1] on peg 2.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recognize Classic Single-Peg Configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Detect when all disks start stacked on a single peg and the goal is the same ordered stack on another peg; in this case the classic recursive solution for the Tower of Hanoi applies directly, yielding the minimal 2^n‑1 moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial state has one peg containing the full ordered tower and the goal is that tower on a different peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Starting with all disks on peg 0 and goal on peg 2 triggers the classic solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Generate Moves Recursively with Explicit Disk IDs
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Use a recursive function that, for k disks, first generates the move sequence for k‑1 disks, then records the move of the kth disk as [disk_id, from_peg, to_peg], and finally generates the moves for the k‑1 disks again. Explicitly tracking disk IDs yields a clear, verifiable move list.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When implementing an algorithm to produce the full sequence of moves for any Tower of Hanoi sub‑problem.
tower-of-hanoi.example: A function move(k, src, dst, aux) that appends [k, src, dst] after recursively moving k‑1 disks.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Violating size rule: moving a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may focus on moving a particular disk without checking the top disk on the destination peg, leading to illegal placement.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always verify that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before committing the move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk without clearing the path.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the topmost disk can be moved, especially when a target disk is buried under smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving any disk, ensure it is the topmost on its peg; if not, first relocate all disks above it.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Final configuration does not match the goal state.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may generate a legal sequence that stops short of the goal or misplaces a disk, resulting in a mismatched final state.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After generating the move list, simulate the entire sequence and compare the resulting configuration with the goal; add missing moves if needed.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Incorrect peg indexing (off‑by‑one or swapped pegs).
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may confuse 0‑based indexing required by the verifier with a 1‑based mental model, leading to wrong peg numbers.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Consistently use 0‑based indexing throughout and double‑check each move’s source and destination peg numbers against the current state.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Premature placement of small disks on the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a small disk onto the goal peg early, forgetting that larger disks still need to be placed underneath, which later makes those moves illegal.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Follow the “Do Not Prematurely Place Small Disks on Goal” principle: only place a small disk onto the goal after all larger required disks are already fixed there.
